top_signal.title: Business partner fiduciary and contract breach
top_signal.summary: Hi - i have a small contracting business and had been working with a guy who I made a partner last year. He was a great employee and had a great attitude up until he was in charge on jobsites - then everything changed.   He quickly mis-quoted a project, then another one and all of a sudden we had lost ~$60k.    Because I needed someone with his skillset, and he kept insisting we would make it back, i kept him on. The business is very short on resources and even more so because of his 6 months of losses.   This summer I drew up and had him sign a contract that effectively made him a fiduciary and personally liable for business losses, on top of him already owing the business based on capital account balance. I was the sole determinant on if he was doing a good job. I told him basically if he can’t agree to these terms I couldn’t continue.    He asked for one concession which I granted because i’m trying to make this work.   I started getting jobs lined up for this fall, and on the first one he decided to set the project up weirdly, and then just didn’t show up the next day, leaving me and a new hire with a mess. I told him he had a fiduciary obligation to the company (given he was in charge of onsite responsibilities.   He added a snarky text comment to let me know he was going home after not showing up for the first 6 hours of the day.
